title: LS-SVM KKT systems and ridge leave-one-out
summary: Connect regularized least squares, dual variables, KKT linear systems, and the efficient leave-one-out residual formula.
objectives: Write the LS-SVM KKT block system
Use the hat matrix for LOO

sourceRefs.role: past-exam dual ridge and LOO alignment

sections.title: Textbook depth · Ridge normal equations
sections.body: Ridge solves $\min_w\frac12\lVert\Phi w-y\rVert^2+\frac\lambda2\lVert w\rVert^2$. Differentiation gives $(\Phi^\top\Phi+\lambda I)\hat w=\Phi^\top y$. The $\lambda I$ term makes the system invertible for $\lambda>0$ even when the design matrix is rank deficient.

math.explanation: Ridge trades fit for a stable, small-norm solution. In a kernel representation the same idea acts through the Gram matrix.

sections.title: Assessment bridge · LS-SVM KKT system
sections.body: A least-squares SVM uses equality constraints with squared errors: $y_i(w^\top\phi(x_i)+b)=1-e_i$ and objective $\frac12\lVert w\rVert^2+\frac\gamma2\sum_i e_i^2$. Stationarity gives $w=\sum_i\alpha_i y_i\phi(x_i)$, $\sum_i\alpha_i y_i=0$, and $\alpha_i=\gamma e_i$.

math.explanation: The block system couples the bias equality with the kernel Gram matrix. It is a linear system rather than the inequality-constrained hard-margin SVM QP.

sections.title: Textbook depth · Hat matrix and LOO
sections.body: For a linear smoother $\hat y=Hy$, the diagonal $H_{ii}$ measures how much observation i influences its own fitted value. Leave-one-out residuals can be computed without refitting as $e_i^{LOO}=e_i/(1-H_{ii})$, where $e_i=y_i-\hat y_i$.

math.explanation: High-leverage points have Hii near one and can make the LOO residual large. The formula is a computational shortcut, not permission to use the test set for tuning.

sections.title: Assessment habit · Compare constraint types
sections.body: Hard-margin SVM has inequality constraints and complementary slackness. LS-SVM replaces them with equality constraints and squared errors, producing a block linear system. Ridge has no margin labels but shares the regularized linear-algebra pattern.

examples.title: Read the LS-SVM block system
steps: The top row enforces y^T alpha=0, which is the bias stationarity condition.
The lower block couples b, alpha, and the kernel matrix through yb+(K+gamma^-1 I)alpha=1.
Solve the block system, then predict with f(x)=sum_i alpha_i y_i k(x_i,x)+b.
examples.answer: The matrix form is the compact answer; explain where each block came from if the question asks for a derivation.

examples.title: LOO residual
steps: Suppose a fitted residual is e_i=0.2 and the leverage is H_ii=0.5.
A high leverage value inflates the correction because the observation strongly affected its own fitted value.
examples.answer: LOO estimates the error after removing point i without fitting N separate models.

criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: Phi transpose Phi is positive semidefinite; adding lambda I shifts every eigenvalue by lambda, making the matrix positive definite for lambda>0.

criticalQuestions.prompt: How is LS-SVM different from hard-margin SVM?
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: LS-SVM uses equality constraints with squared error slack and yields a block linear system; hard-margin SVM uses inequalities, nonnegative multipliers, and complementary slackness.
